review_scope: Installed hook registration, first-throw input, replication boundary, equipment/loadout copying and SCIS/VSS resource/scope lifecycle; final camera callback guards.
conclusions: InputDispatch enters sticky-camera input, but a nondeployed camera does not meet the state-2 selection gate and continues through native input dispatch. This does not exclude the plugin: Tick/Cleanup/Disable and shared resource/pawn lifecycle hooks remain actual intersections.

The camera registry installs Whistle, WhistleSend, Receive, Tick, Cleanup and Disable. Receive calls the native handler under a receive marker. No direct first-throw constructor or generic actor/component-copy replacement was identified in the reviewed registrations.

SCIS/VSS register_with_copy copies exact XML weapon/attachment catalog records. Extended-loadout cloning and upgrade assignment copy loadout values. Neither is a demonstrated StickyCam actor-replication implementation.

SCIS/VSS archetype routing and geometry retries are restricted to named weapons and five geometry keys. The generic model builder still intercepts native calls; AScope1stPerson creation and pawn/scope destruction can intersect equipment changes. Source scoping does not prove runtime lifecycle safety or a cause of the reported crash.

Candidate gameplay enables default extended-player-capacity plus goggle-feedback; its build does not pass --no-default-features. The separately retained network-rate boost is temporarily disabled. Neither observation establishes a cause of the four-peer deployment incident.

Final Detonate code rechecks READY and the original Owner after both native availability and sound cancellation. The reviewed fixture invokes production execute with one healthy control and four destruction/replacement controls, using synthetic native leaves. This review did not execute it.
No additional confirmed source defect or causal link to the reported Access=8 / Instruction=0 deployment crash was established. The separate Access=1 / RVA 0x20c25b4 write fault remains separate.
open_boundaries: A complete admitted retail first-throw, constructor, component-clone or replication body and a credible failing return callsite were not identified in the reviewed references. Small signature bytes and function hashes are not such a fixture.
Tick/Cleanup/Disable callback lifetime, generic resource building, pawn/scope destruction, actual resource GC and real native execution order remain unverified for the incident.
Existing +0x20 object index is not a proven allocation generation; same-address/same-index reuse and concurrent cross-thread release remain unproven.
Synthetic audio, original Whistle, sender, availability and trigger leaves do not execute real deployment, actor replication, ATS effects, audio hardware or network delivery.
The 13 historical authored listings are not complete native replay inputs; this review does not replace C71 or constitute an exhaustive audit of all plugin code.
